load_extension_reason: Initial 72 bounded units completed while substantive derived work remained available; extension is useful analysis, not idle padding.
analysis: A workload-unit count is not itself a duration proxy; timing classification must use timestamps.
Repository round trips exercise I/O and checkpoint paths relevant to the relay workload.
Frequent immutable checkpoints reduce evidence loss but add overhead; this overhead is part of the tested workload profile.
Strict duration evidence should record workload profile so later universal-cap claims can test heterogeneous profiles.
If this invocation terminates before durable close near target without an independent failure, classification must consider duration_fail rather than silently retry.
If useful work exhausts again before target, classification remains under_target and the generator must be enlarged rather than treating it as a pass/fail.
The successor wake at START+17m intentionally leaves a +3m planned gap relative to target, preserving the current baseline while runtime is isolated.
Once a boundary is found, planned-gap optimization can reduce actual idle time independently.
Long-run utilization depends jointly on active duration, close reliability, wake jitter, and planned gap; maximizing nominal duration alone is insufficient.
A failed final checkpoint can dominate the utilization benefit of a longer target, motivating repeated cap validation.
The decision rule correctly distinguishes exploratory lower-bound advancement from production-cap promotion.
Parallel overlap remains a later optimization because it changes scheduler/control conditions and would confound strict boundary evidence now.
